target_customer: Central Valley agricultural water districts (irrigation drainage), later consumers, businesses and cities through a water marketplace
problem: Agricultural drainage water and brackish sources need cheaper, sustainable treatment than energy-hungry reverse osmosis.
business_model: Water treatment project developer selling treated water, later a marketplace with water credits
product_category: Solar thermal desalination and water marketplace

founders.name: Aaron Mandell
founders.role: Co-founder and Chairman (listed as founder on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Press Democrat (2015-07-19) says he helped start about six companies and moved to Healdsburg around 2013. YC page describes a background in groundwater hydrology and computational modeling. Education not found.

competitors.name: Trevi Systems
competitors.what: Petaluma company focused on brackish groundwater desalination
competitors.traction_then: mentioned as another Sonoma County desalination approach

competitors.name: Reverse osmosis incumbents
competitors.what: Prevailing desalination technology in the field
competitors.traction_then: the dominant method per the article

technical_complexity.rationale: A solar-heated mineral oil desalination plant needs thermal engineering, a pilot at about 10 gallons per minute, environmental review and a $30 million build, which is hard for a four person team.

defensibility.rationale: Trademarks on AQUA4 and HYDROREVOLUTION and site-specific projects gave some protection, but the process was unproven at scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it according to sources found; the company later pivoted to a different technology and marketplace.

market_need_then: California drought and irrigation drainage contamination in the Central Valley created demand; the company had a $1M state grant for its pilot near Firebaugh (2015) and planned a $30M plant.

branding.domain_note: Later operates as wacomet.com under the Wacomet Water name

identity.visual_style: A design agency Behance case study says it built a visual identity and website for Wacomet
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission language about reimagining water for ten billion people

branding.brand_signature: Liquid, the peer to peer water distribution platform name

rebrands.why: not stated; the product moved from the Aqua4 solar thermal plant to solvent extraction desalination and a water marketplace

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade press in 2015 and trademarks on product names, but no sign of a recognized brand or community; renamed later.

pivots.from: Aqua4 solar thermal desalination of irrigation drainage
pivots.to: Wacomet Water, solvent extraction desalination with a blockchain-recorded water marketplace
pivots.why: not stated by sources; date of the change not found

outcome_analysis: WaterFX built a trial solar desalination plant near Firebaugh with a $1 million state grant and in 2015 offered $10 million of preferred stock to Californians to fund a $30 million plant. YC lists it inactive, yet the company continues as Wacomet Water with a new technology and marketplace, so the record is a pivot or dormant successor rather than a confirmed shutdown. No source explains why the original plant plan stalled, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: The $10 million HydroRevolution preferred stock offering (CleanTechnica 2015-09-10) is an offering, not a confirmed raise, so it is not recorded as a round. The 2018-03-08 angel round with Thomas Middleditch rests on a single database (CB Insights, which also reports $3M over 2 rounds total, so at least one round is missing). The $1M state grant date is not given; the plant was built before July 2015. Competitor sources are dated 2015, two years before the batch, and no 2017 dated rival source was found. Exit: YC lists Inactive but the Wacomet Water website is live, so exit type is unknown and the conflict is unresolved. Founded year 2012 from CB Insights and the 2015 article saying about three years old.
